title: DCPSC Order No. 23128 (2026-07-23) — The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. EA11-19, by Order No. 23128, dated July 23, 2026, granted the request of Viridian
description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. EA11-19, by Order No. 23128, dated July 23, 2026, granted the request of Viridian Energy PA, LLC (“Viridian” or “Applicant”) to surrender its electricity supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s electricity supplier license is effective upon the issuance of this Order.

FORMAL CASE NO. EA11-19, IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF

LICENSE IN THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, Order No. 23128 
I.
INTRODUCTION
1.
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia
(“Commission”) grants the request of Viridian Energy PA, LLC (“Viridian” or “Applicant”) to 
surrender its electricity supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s electricity supplier license 
is effective upon the issuance of this Order. 
II.
BACKGROUND
2.
On July 12, 2011, the Commission granted Viridian a license to operate as an
electricity supplier in the District of Columbia (“District”) in Order No. 16446.2 On June 5, 2026, 
Viridian filed an Application with the Commission to surrender its electricity supplier license.3 
Viridian was approved to operate as a marketer of electricity services, but it conducts no business 
and has no customers in the District.4 Consequently, Viridian requests to surrender its electricity 
supplier license.5 
1

the Matter of the Investigation into the Public Service Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Order 
No. 21981, ¶ 2. (m), issued April 24, 2024 (“The Commission’s General Counsel, or his or her designee, is delegated 
authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . m. Applications for the Abandonment of Gas or Electric 
Licenses”). Any party may file a petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the Commission.

III.
DISCUSSION
3.
According to 15 DCMR § 4602.10 (a)(1), a licensed electricity supplier wishing to
cease providing services in the District is required to provide written notice to the Commission of 
the licensee’s intention to cease providing electricity service to its customers and inform its 
customers of the choice to revert to the default service provider or another electricity supplier. 
Section 4602.10 (a)(2) also requires that the surrendering licensee provide to the Commission an 
example or copy of the notice it provided to its customers and, upon the Commission’s receipt of 
such notice, may order the licensee to provide such further notice to its customers or the public as 
the Commission deems necessary, and/or take such other action that the Commission considers 
appropriate.6 
4.
In the instant case, Viridian’s Application provides the required notice to the
Commission of its intention to surrender its electricity supplier license.7 Viridian also states that 
the notice requirement to customers is not applicable because it has no customers in the District.8 
Accordingly, Viridian’s Application satisfies the notice requirement with regard to the cessation 
of service. 
5.
In all other respects, Viridian’s Application conforms with Commission
requirements for a surrendering licensee. Commission records confirm the Applicant’s submission 
of the case number, order number, and date the Applicant’s license was granted.9 Viridian avers, 
and Commission records confirm that the Applicant’s most recent survey response indicates no 
jurisdictional revenue and that it owes no outstanding debt or fees.10 In addition, the Applicant 
states that it has no outstanding consumer complaints.11 Lastly, the signed Application from an 
officer of Viridian attests to the truth and accuracy of the information submitted.12 
6.
Based upon the preceding information, the Commission grants Viridian’s request
to surrender its electricity supplier license granted by Order No. 16446. Cancellation of Viridian’s 
electricity supplier license shall become effective upon the issuance of this Order. Should Viridian 
seek to re-enter the District’s electricity market in the future, it shall have to reapply for an 
electricity supplier license pursuant to Chapter 46 of the Commission’s rules. 
6
See 15 DCMR § 4602.10 (2022): Cessation of Business in the District of Columbia or Cessation of Business 
to a Customer Class.
